title: Private install environment assessor and quota intelligence
creator: Ava Morgan
description: Build an automated 'environment assessor' that performs end-to-end pre-install checks for Private (VPC) installs. The assessor will validate cloud quotas, IAM roles/policies, cluster networking (DNS & routing), and GPU capacity profiles before any terraform apply / operator bootstrap step. This ticket covers the design, Terraform integration points, implementation of a CLI/web check, and a lightweight health-check api used by the installer to fail fast with actionable remediation steps. Goal: reduce install failures during customer Private on-boarding by surfacing exact missing permissions or insufficient quota and provide deterministic remediation guidance.
acceptance_criteria: CLI 'ri-assess env' command runs against a target cloud account and returns structured findings with severity (blocker/warning/info)

Checks include: IAM role bindings & required managed policies, service account scopes, VPC quota and subnet availability, DNS/Route53 or CloudDNS write permissions, GPU SKU availability and per-region GPU quota, and keypair/KMS accessibility
Terraform integration: assessor can use terraform state and data sources where available, but falls back to cloud provider APIs when state is not present
Installer blocks progression on any 'blocker' findings and surfaces user-friendly remediation instructions in the Console and CLI
Automated unit/integration tests for each check and a fuzzer test that intentionally misconfigures permissions to ensure correct failure categories
implementation_notes: We will implement provider-agnostic check modules (aws/gcp/azure) that expose a common result schema (id, severity, message, remediation_links)
Prefer minimal-permission read-only API calls for checks. Where we need additional lookups (eg. list regions for GPU SKUs), batch requests and respect provider rate limits
For terraform-enabled installs, prefer using the TF state and provider credentials in order to check resource-specific settings (eg. vpc id, subnet ids) before elevating to a wider cloud account scan
GPU availability check: map requested instance types to provider SKU names and query region-level availability + quota. Flag soft-limits vs hard-disabled SKUs
DNS checks: perform both IAM permission checks (canChangeRecordSets) and a synthetic write test against a temporary subdomain to verify propagation permissions where network routing allows

IAM policy checks: expand managed policy lists and detect policies that would block our installer (eg. explicit Deny on ec2:RunInstances, iam:CreateServiceLinkedRole), produce the minimal required permission set in remediation

Trade-offs: We debated fully agent-based deep scans vs. ephemeral API-only checks. Chose API-first approach to avoid requiring extra infra in customer accounts; will add optional agent later for network path validation behind private subnets
runbook: Step 1: User runs 'ri-assess env --cloud aws --region us-west-2 --tfstate s3://... --output json'
Step 2: Assessor collects TF state (if provided), validates provider creds, enumerates VPC/subnets, then sequentially runs checks: IAM -> Quota -> DNS -> GPU -> KMS
Step 3: For each blocker, assessor returns remediation text with sample terraform code snippets or console instructions
Rollback: If an installer proceeds despite warnings and the install fails, the installer should log the failing assessor id and surface the original assessor output in the incident
Operator alerting: failed preflight (blocker) increments a metric 'preflight.blocker.count' with tags (cloud,region,team) to monitor common customer pain points
test_plan: Unit tests for each provider check using recorded provider fixtures (vcr-style)
Integration harness that spins up minimal test accounts in sandbox org (quota-limited) and runs negative tests by removing permissions
Load test to ensure assessor completes within 45s for accounts with up to 50 subnets and 20 attached policies
E2E smoke: run with sample tfstate from onboarding repo and ensure installer blocks on the blocker list
